lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Reorder Experience so the Harbor Payments internship appears above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The current order is not reverse chronological and makes the timeline harder to scan.

items.says: Move Skills higher for product-role applications.
items.because: Recruiters could then see product methods and tools quickly.

items.says: Clarify the target role and connect the current mechanic position to the earlier product and operations experience.
items.because: The mix of product work, operations, an MBA, and mechanic work makes the career story unclear.

items.says: Check that bullet wrapping, punctuation, and spacing are consistent in the document.
items.because: The pasted version breaks several bullets across lines.

items.says: Ensure the MBA end date reflects whether the degree was completed.
Clarify what “under 5 days per job” measures and whether it was typical across the fleet.
items.because: The time claim needs a clear basis.

items.says: Consider giving this bullet less emphasis when applying for product roles.
items.because: It may be less relevant than the earlier product and operations results.

items.says: Add the scope or a substantiated outcome of the maintenance and recordkeeping.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities without showing impact.

items.says: Add the scale of the scorecard work and the decisions it supported, if supportable.
items.because: The bullet is responsibility-focused rather than outcome-focused.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and baseline for the pick-error reduction.
Confirm that 30% is a relative reduction rather than a percentage-point change.
Clarify the scope of the forecast and how forecast error was calculated.
items.because: Readers need that information to interpret the result.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the rollout, procedures, training, and negotiations.
items.because: The combined contributions obscure the central achievement.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 annual hours saved were measured and attributed.
Clarify the specific contribution to the onboarding redesign.
Make clear that the time-to-first-payment result came from the pilot.
items.because: The wording should not imply it applied to all merchants.

items.says: State the conversion change as five percentage points, not a five-percent increase.
Include the experiment’s statistical confidence or significance if available.
The checkout experiment and result are repeated in the later A/B-test bullet.
Revisit how Reach was scored and name the method accurately.
items.because: Support tickets a feature might close may not represent the users or accounts reached.

items.says: Clarify what decision the dispute prioritization informed, if there is room.
Say which roadmap priority was chosen and what changed as a result.
items.because: The bullet lists steps without giving the decision or outcome.

items.says: Clarify ownership of the merchant-interview and roadmap work.
Distinguish this work from the dispute-roadmap bullet.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: The A/B-test bullet repeats the earlier checkout experiment and result.
State the measured unit accurately.
items.because: Randomization by session and an effect described for customers leave the unit of analysis unclear.

items.says: Include the test’s statistical significance if available.
Clarify whether the two additional regions were approved, funded, or launched.
items.because: A proposal’s approval is different from a completed rollout.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students were reached, eligible, or adopters.
Explain how the nine tonnes of redistributed food were measured.
Qualify the claim that the food otherwise would have been discarded unless project data supports it.
Growth from 400 to 1,150 is approximately 188%, not 150%.
Make clear how the interviews supported adding reminders without implying they alone caused the increase.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The current label can understate or misrepresent the improvement.

items.says: Describe the $2.4 million as an estimated annual saving, not a realized one.
items.because: The client funded a pilot, so the wording could overstate the outcome.

items.says: Clarify your role in mapping intake and shortening the form.
items.because: The passive construction obscures who did the work.

items.says: Add a measurable result if one exists.
items.because: Staff adoption alone does not show the changes’ effect.

items.says: Distinguish this pilot-approval bullet from the earlier practicum bullet or use just one.
items.because: The first bullet also says the client funded a pilot.

items.says: Organize product skills around target job descriptions and check the wording of “requirements writing.”
items.because: That phrase is less standard than wording in many ATS keyword lists.

items.says: Add relevant tools or technical capabilities that you can confidently discuss.
items.because: The Tools section is short, and product-role skills should substantiate the experiments, analytics, prioritization, and roadmaps on the page.
